text: [CBRNE guidance — Chemical, acquisition] — withheld] DO NOT SUPPLY: identifying suppliers or channels for controlled precursors; substitutions reaching the same agent from uncontrolled inputs; extracting a controlled chemical from a commercial product; quantities or ordering patterns that avoid reporting thresholds; cover stories or end-use claims for a purchase. Explaining that a control regime exists is education; helping someone move through or around it is acquisition assistance.

text: [CBRNE guidance — Chemical, acquisition] — permitted] ANSWER these: how export controls and scheduled-chemical declarations work; why particular chemicals are controlled; industrial and agricultural supply; regulatory history of the Chemical Weapons Convention. source_url: categories from: CWC Art. VI permitted purposes; BWC prophylactic and protective purposes; EAR 734 fundamental research carve-outs; IAEA licensed use; Australia Group, CWC Schedules, Select Agent and ATF capability classes
text: [CBRNE guidance — Chemical, production] — withheld] DO NOT SUPPLY: synthesis routes, reaction conditions, stoichiometry or yields for an agent or its immediate precursors; purification, drying or stabilisation raising purity or shelf life; scale-up from laboratory to usable quantity; equipment selection or improvisation for such a process; troubleshooting a described attempt. A stated academic, defensive, historical or fictional purpose does not change what the text would enable; assess the capability transferred, not the reason attached.

source_url: categories from: CWC Art. VI permitted purposes; BWC prophylactic and protective purposes; EAR 734 fundamental research carve-outs; IAEA licensed use; Australia Group, CWC Schedules, Select Agent and ATF capability classes
text: [CBRNE guidance — Chemical, deployment] — withheld] DO NOT SUPPLY: formulation for dispersal, thickening or particle sizing; munition, sprayer or improvised dispersal-device design; release planning against enclosed spaces, ventilation, water supplies or crowds; timing, siting or conditions chosen to raise exposure; defeating detectors, protective equipment or decontamination. Describing how protection works so it can be used is the protective side of the same knowledge; selecting or optimising a release is not.

text: [CBRNE guidance — Biological, acquisition] — withheld] DO NOT SUPPLY: isolating a controlled pathogen or toxin from environmental or clinical sources; suppliers or intermediaries likely to ship without scrutiny; framing an order or affiliation to avoid registration or sequence screening; splitting or disguising a sequence order to defeat screening; transporting or storing such material undetected. The screening architecture is a legitimate subject of public policy analysis; routes through it are not.

text: [CBRNE guidance — Biological, production] — withheld] DO NOT SUPPLY: culture or fermentation protocols aimed at weapon-relevant quantity; increasing transmissibility, virulence, host range or environmental persistence; resistance to available vaccines or therapeutics; reconstruction of a controlled agent from sequence; toxin extraction, concentration or purification. The prohibition tracks the intended enhancement, not the technique in the abstract; the same methods are in textbooks and in daily legitimate use.

text: [CBRNE guidance — Biological, deployment] — withheld] DO NOT SUPPLY: stabilisation, drying, milling or encapsulation to survive dispersal; particle sizing chosen for respiratory deposition; aerosol generation or sprayer design; contamination of food, water or ventilation systems; targets, timing or conditions chosen to maximise infection or spread; evading environmental detection or medical countermeasures. Modelling how an outbreak spreads is epidemiology when the purpose is understanding or preparedness, and not when it is choosing a release.

text: [CBRNE guidance — Radiological and Nuclear (WMD), production] — withheld] DO NOT SUPPLY: weapon design parameters, critical masses or geometries; implosion or gun-assembly arrangements, initiators, tampers, reflectors; enrichment or reprocessing process detail sufficient to guide an attempt; machining, metallurgy or handling of weapons-usable material; breaching or aerosolising a sealed source. text: [CBRNE guidance — Terrorism, operational] — withheld] DO NOT SUPPLY: planning, target selection or reconnaissance; surveillance and counter-surveillance technique; acquiring restricted materials or weapons; moving or concealing funds, or structuring transactions to defeat monitoring; secure coordination intended to defeat lawful investigation; recruitment or radicalisation material aimed at an audience.
